sources.name: LIDAR Composite Digital Terrain Model (DTM) - 1m
verified_facts: The composite DTM is a raster elevation model covering approximately 99% of England at 1m spatial resolution.
Surface objects are removed to produce a terrain-only model; where repeat surveys exist the newest, best-resolution data is used.
Resampled inputs use bilinear interpolation; the published vertical accuracy is plus or minus 15cm RMSE and the horizontal CRS is EPSG:27700.
semantic_limits: One-metre spatial resolution is grid spacing, not a guarantee of one independent ground observation per pixel.
Published RMSE is dataset-level accuracy evidence and does not replace exact parcel-polygon sampling and readback.

sources.name: LIDAR DTM Time Stamped Tiles
verified_facts: Time-stamped DTM tiles are supplied as GeoTIFF rasters in 5km zip files with elevations in metres.
Data is referenced to Ordnance Datum Newlyn and aligned to the OS Grid.
Published vertical accuracy is plus or minus 15cm RMSE and the transformation used depends on the survey period.
semantic_limits: Survey-date transformation provenance must be retained when mixing tiles or comparing releases.
ODN reference and RMSE do not prove the exact min/max values for any candidate parcel.

sources.name: OS Terrain 5 grid data
verified_facts: Each Terrain 5 raster value is calculated as the mean height across the whole 5m pixel.
ASCII grid z values are positioned at pixel centres, 2.5m from the tile edge, and each tile contains 1000 by 1000 pixels.
Height values are supplied as real values to the nearest 0.01m.
semantic_limits: Centimetre numeric precision is not centimetre terrain accuracy.
A five-metre pixel mean is not a point observation and remains secondary evidence for sub-metre parcel differences.

sources.name: Practice guide 40 supplement 3: boundaries
verified_facts: An exact legal boundary is rarely identified precisely on the ground or in conveyances and is not shown by Ordnance Survey mapping.
Title plans show the general position rather than the exact line of boundaries.
Plans may be subject to scale distortion and scaled measurements may not match measurements on the ground.
semantic_limits: An INSPIRE or title-plan polygon must not be represented as a surveyed legal boundary.
Height sampling can describe terrain inside the selected polygon geometry but cannot determine legal ownership limits.
